name: adaptive-practice — explain, then route on grounded

meta.description: ⚠️ THE BRANCH IS THE POINT. POST /explain returns `grounded`, and a grounded answer goes straight to the candidate while an abstention is routed to a human queue. That is the product decision this repository is built around: a tutor that cannot abstain will invent an explanation, and a candidate who is told they misunderstood something they did not is worse off than one who is told nothing.

env.API_BASE: e.g. http://host.docker.internal:8000 — from inside the container, localhost is the container
env.QUEUE_URL: where an abstention is enqueued for a human, e.g. http://host.docker.internal:8001/queue

nodes.name: Webhook
nodes.notes: POST /webhook/practice — body: {candidate_id, item_id, chosen, attempts, day}

nodes.name: Explain
nodes.notes: ⚠️ `chosen` is validated server-side to a single option letter. A malformed value is a 422, not a silent default — which is why the branch below can trust `grounded`.

nodes.name: Grounded?
nodes.notes: ⚠️⚠️ THE DECISION THIS WORKFLOW EXISTS TO MAKE. `grounded` comes from the retrieval gate, not from a model's self-report — a model asked whether it is confident answers yes.

nodes.name: Recommend
nodes.notes: ⚠️ Reached ONLY when the corpus supports an answer. The next item follows an explanation the candidate can actually rely on.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ kind: 'abstention', item_id: $('Webhook').item.json.body.item_id, chosen: $('Webhook').item.json.body.chosen, candidate_id: $('Webhook').item.json.body.candidate_id || 'anonymous', reason: $json.reason, needs: 'a subject expert must decide whether this question is in scope' }) }}

nodes.name: Queue for human review
nodes.notes: ⚠️ An abstention is a QUEUE ITEM, not an error. It is the signal that the syllabus does not cover a question a candidate was asked — which is a content gap for a human to close, and the most valuable thing this workflow emits.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ grounded: true, explanation: $('Explain').item.json.explanation, citations: $('Explain').item.json.citations, next_item: $json.item_id, basis: $json.basis, note: $json.note }) }}
={{ JSON.stringify({ grounded: false, abstained: true, explanation: $('Explain').item.json.explanation, queued_for_review: true, reason: $('Explain').item.json.reason }) }}

nodes.name: Respond — abstained
nodes.notes: ⚠️ 200, not 500. An abstention is a correct outcome, not a failure — and a client that treats it as an error will retry it, which is how a content gap becomes an outage.
